starter.7-10: God, thank you for today. I am happy because…
starter.11-14: God, today has been good. Thank you for…
starter.15-18: God, I want to name what is good today rather than take it for granted…

reflection.7-10: Happy days are good days to say thank you.
reflection.11-14: Gratitude is easiest today — which is exactly why today is worth using for it.
reflection.15-18: Thanksgiving in good times is practice for trusting the same God in worse ones.

starter.11-14: God, I don't really want to talk about it, but…
starter.15-18: God, I am not going to pretend I am fine…

reflection.7-10: God does not mind you being sad. He comes close when you are.
reflection.11-14: Half the psalms are complaints. Sadness is not something to hide from God — it is something to bring.
reflection.15-18: Lament is a biblical genre, not a failure of faith. Jesus wept at a grave he was about to open.

starter.11-14: God, this is the thing going round and round in my head…
starter.15-18: God, here is what I keep rehearsing instead of sleeping…

reflection.7-10: You can tell God the thing you are scared about. He is listening.
reflection.11-14: Paul does not say stop feeling anxious. He says do something specific with it — name it to God.
reflection.15-18: Naming an anxiety in prayer is not the same as solving it. The promise attached is peace that guards, not an explanation.

starter.11-14: God, this made me angry, and I think it was unfair because…
starter.15-18: God, I am angry, and I would rather bring it to you than take it out on someone…

reflection.7-10: Being angry is not naughty. What you do next matters.
reflection.11-14: 'Be angry and do not sin' assumes anger is coming. It is about what happens in the next ten minutes.
reflection.15-18: Scripture treats anger as morally serious in both directions — as a signal about injustice and as a danger to the one carrying it.

starter.7-10: God, I am tired. Please help me…
starter.11-14: God, I am running out of energy for…
starter.15-18: God, I am tired in a way sleep has not fixed…

reflection.7-10: Jesus says: come to me and I will give you rest.
reflection.11-14: Jesus offers rest to people who are already carrying something, not to people with nothing to do.
reflection.15-18: The sabbath logic is that rest is a creational good and a trust exercise, not a reward for finishing.

starter.11-14: God, three things I am grateful for today…
starter.15-18: God, I want to be specific rather than general about this…

reflection.7-10: Saying thank you helps you notice good things.
reflection.11-14: Gratitude is a skill. Being specific is what turns it from a habit into attention.
reflection.15-18: Psalm 103 addresses the self — 'bless the Lord, O my soul' — because thanksgiving often has to be commanded before it is felt.

starter.11-14: God, I am not sure what I think about…
starter.15-18: God, I have a question I am not sure I am allowed to ask…

reflection.7-10: It is alright not to understand. You can ask God about it.
reflection.11-14: 'I believe; help my unbelief' is in the Bible because someone actually said it — and Jesus answered him.
reflection.15-18: Doubt handled honestly tends to produce sturdier faith than doubt suppressed. James's promise of wisdom is offered without reproach.
